claims.explanation: NSC-663284 is a quinone-based Cdc25 inhibitor that also redox cycles to generate reactive oxygen species, and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on Cdc25A/B/C and/or sensitivity to oxidative stress. Lines with high Cdc25 expression or KEAP1/NFE2L2 pathway mutations that impair antioxidant responses may be more sensitive, while intact antioxidant capacity or low Cdc25 dependence may protect.

features.basis: NSC-663284 directly inhibits Cdc25A (Ki 29 nM); high expression may increase dependence
NSC-663284 is most selective for Cdc25B (Ki 95 nM) and inhibits it in cells
NSC-663284 inhibits Cdc25C (Ki 89 nM) and blocks Cdk1 activation
Damaging KEAP1 mutations impair antioxidant response, enhancing quinone-induced ROS toxicity; observed in sensitive HEC265
NFE2L2 mutations may dysregulate antioxidant response; observed in sensitive HEC265 and MFE319 (though MFE319 is resistant, suggesting context dependence)
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines and may impair DNA damage/apoptosis response, but also common in resistant lines
BRAF mutations observed in several sensitive melanoma and thyroid lines, but also in resistant lines
PTEN loss may increase oxidative stress sensitivity; observed in sensitive WM793 and JHUEM2
ARID1A mutations are enriched in resistant lines (e.g., NCIH1793, MDAMB361, EFE184, SNU449)
KRAS mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but several resistant lines harbor KRAS (ASPC1, GSU, OV7, LS1034)
SMARCA4 mutations observed in resistant lines (NCIH1793, OV7, PLCPRF5 is sensitive though)
ATM mutations may impair DNA damage response; observed in sensitive 8305C and resistant 786O
